rules.disease: Pulmonary Atresia with Ventricular Septal Defect
rules.sentence: In PAVSD, the degree of pulmonary artery involvement steers the clinical picture and the treatment options.

rules.disease: Pulmonary Atresia with Ventricular Septal Defect
rules.sentence: Presentations include an isolated valvular atresia or proximal pulmonary trunk involvement.

rules.disease: Pulmonary Atresia with Ventricular Septal Defect
rules.sentence: The right and left pulmonary arteries may or may not communicate, and the intrapericardial pulmonary arteries are often very diminutive (1 to 3 mm).[8]

rules.disease: Pulmonary Atresia with Ventricular Septal Defect
rules.sentence: MAPCAs usually supply the lung parenchyma; these MAPCAs may arise from the thoracic or abdominal aorta, subclavian arteries, internal mammary arteries, intercostal arteries, or other less common locations.

rules.disease: Pulmonary Atresia with Ventricular Septal Defect
rules.sentence: The systemic-to-pulmonary anastomoses in MAPCAs are classified into extrapulmonary, hilar, lobar, and segmental.

rules.disease: Pulmonary Atresia with Ventricular Septal Defect
rules.sentence: MAPCAs are usually aberrant and stenosed at either end.
